transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-27
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 9 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Dev Patel (Redwood SE); Aminah Farouk (Zenova Partnerships); Luis Ortega (Zenova Head of Cloud Partnerships); Samir Kapoor (Zenova SE)

Summary: informal partner intro + discovery; notes on private deployment options, GPU SKUs, networking, and a potential pilot.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this, and with me is Dev our solutions engineer, hi Dev.
00:07 - Dev Patel: Hey, hi all, nice to meet you, thanks for carving out time.
00:12 - Aminah Farouk: Thanks, Maya, excited to chat, we had a quick note from Luis that Zenova is exploring more deeper partnerships to expand GPU capacity and also provide a managed experience for customers.
00:24 - Luis Ortega: Yeah, uh we're seeing customers ask for integrated stacks, like they want a managed LLM service with predictable latency and cost, but also tight network controls. We're curious about Redwood's partner models.
00:36 - Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly — Redwood has a few partner models, we do reseller, we also have integration partner options. On the technical side we support hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private -- the private option can be deployed in a customer's VPC or on-prem.
00:57 - Samir Kapoor: Quick q, sorry, is Redwood Private a separate control plane or do you run the control plane in our cloud?
01:03 - Dev Patel: Good question, yeah so Redwood Private is flexible: we can run a customer-managed control plane in their VPC, or deliver an on-prem bundle. It's a little dependent on compliance needs. Sometimes the naming gets butchered in the docs — people call it 'Redwood Privet' — but it's the private control plane.
01:19 - Aminah Farouk: Ha, yeah we've seen the 'Privet' typo. From a go-to-market perspective, we're interested in a revenue share vs. resell; also curious about co-sell motion.
01:31 - Maya Chen: Both are possible. For a reseller model we can provide committed Dedicated pools and volume pricing, while integration partners get referral fees and can co-sell with our AE team. We should align on which route fits Zenova's sales motions.
01:45 - Luis Ortega: Most of our customers are enterprises with SOC2 and strict audit needs; they'd likely want VPC peering and customer-managed keys. Can Redwood support KMS integration and HSM?
01:58 - Dev Patel: Yes, we integrate with KMS/HSM providers; for Redwood Private deployments customer-managed KMS is supported and we log key interactions in audit logs. Our security docs cover SOC 2, ISO compliance as well.
02:11 - Samir Kapoor: Dev, on the infra side, what GPU SKUs do you support? Our fleet has A100s and some 80GB GPUs, and we also have a few H100s coming online.
02:23 - Dev Patel: We support a range — from A10G-ish SKUs to A100/80GB and H100. Some customers use our compiled kernels for H100 and there are subtle perf differences. We'll share a compatibility matrix. Also, quantization and memory profile matters for throughput; we can advise on recommended models for each SKUs.
02:46 - Maya Chen: For pilots we usually run a benchmark with a representative prompt set, measure latency and cost at target QPS. Dev will share the benchmark spreadsheet, and we can run an initial test on a small Dedicated pool or on Zenova infra.
03:01 - Luis Ortega: What's typical lead time for Dedicated capacity vs private deployment?
03:07 - Dev Patel: Dedicated can be provisioned in days to a couple of weeks depending on capacity. Private deployments, especially customer-managed VPC + KMS, usually take 2-6 weeks depending on networking approvals.
03:18 - Aminah Farouk: For the pilot, we want to prove predictable p99 latency under mixed workloads. Also need to test prefix caching / KV cache features for our persistent agents product.
03:31 - Dev Patel: Yes, caching and continuous batching are key levers. We can enable prefix/KV caching and configure batch windows — those are tunable. We'll need sample traffic patterns to choose the right batching policy.
03:44 - Maya Chen: Also to call out, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for batching and quant profiles to reduce unit cost. We'll include that in the deck.
03:55 - Luis Ortega: Pricing: do you have list price for dedicated pools and any reseller discounts?
04:02 - Maya Chen: We'll share partner pricing; it varies with commit levels. For pilot we can often offer preferred pilot rates. I'll include a partner pricing sheet.
04:11 - Samir Kapoor: On the networking side, do you support VPC peering and PrivateLink? Some customers require no internet egress for model inferencing.
04:20 - Dev Patel: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink patterns, and isolated deployments. For true air-gapped customers, we deliver an on-prem package — that's heavier but possible.
04:35 - Aminah Farouk: We also want clarity on support SLAs, who's the escalation contact for production incidents when it's a joint deployment.
04:44 - Maya Chen: For Partner deals we provide joint support playbooks. For Dedicated/resell we'll provide an initial SLA, and we can agree on escalation paths. For Private deployments, there's an ops handoff and we can offer managed support add-on.
04:58 - Luis Ortega: Any gotchas regarding model licensing? We have customers that want to run closed-source models, or commercial models with additional licensing constraints.
05:09 - Dev Patel: Licensing is model-dependent. For open models it's straightforward; for commercial models we coordinate license terms. We'll map this out in the pilot SOW.
05:20 - Samir Kapoor: Regarding telemetry and observability, do you expose traces for per-request latency and token-level cost so our ops can correlate?
05:28 - Dev Patel: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, traces, and we can hook to Datadog or send logs to your syslog. We'll make sure the telemetry meets your needs.
05:44 - Aminah Farouk: Great, can we talk briefly about go-to-market and enablement? What partner materials do you provide?
05:51 - Maya Chen: We'll provide co-branded collateral, a partner playbook, sales training, and joint case study templates. For technical enablement, our SEs will run onboarding sessions and we have reference architecture docs.
06:08 - Luis Ortega: We'll need an NDA + MOU for the pilot — typical legal housekeeping.
06:13 - Maya Chen: Yep, we'll send an NDA and a short MOU draft; legal usually turns quickly on pilot MOUs.
06:23 - Dev Patel: Quick technical note: when we do benchmarks, we often test multiple model sizes and check quantized variants — smaller quantized models can reduce memory footprint on A100/80GB and H100 has different kernel optim.
06:39 - Samir Kapoor: I saw mention of 'KV cache' earlier; do you have limits on cache size per host or sharding requirements?
06:47 - Dev Patel: There are limits, but caching is configurable. For very long contexts we stream KV cache across hosts, and there's a tradeoff between latency and memory. We'll share guidance in the kernel compatibility doc.
07:02 - Luis Ortega: What's the expected throughput per GPU for a 1k token request at p50/p95 on H100 vs A100?
07:11 - Dev Patel: Ballpark: on H100 you might see 2-3x throughput over A100 for certain models, but it's model dependent. We'll run specific benchmarks and quantify p50/p95.
07:24 - Maya Chen: I'll also flag that we have a Redwood-verified models list with performance profiles; that should help with sizing.
07:33 - Aminah Farouk: Are there any sample contracts or partner agreement templates we can review?
07:38 - Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach standard partnership templates and a reseller addendum.
07:48 - Luis Ortega: Ok on timelines: if we aim for a pilot kickoff the week of Jan 12th, what do you need from us?
07:55 - Dev Patel: We'll need sample prompt sets, an expected QPS, sample dataset for privacy checks, and GPU SKU inventory. Also access to a staging VPC if you want us to run tests in your environment.
08:10 - Samir Kapoor: We can provide the inventory and sample prompts, and we can provision a staging VPC; I'll own that.
08:16 - Aminah Farouk: I'll coordinate the legal + commercial side.
08:20 - Maya Chen: Perfect. So next steps recap: Maya sends partner deck, Dev shares benchmark sheet, Samir shares GPU inventory, and we'll schedule technical deep dive next Tue.
08:34 - Luis Ortega: One more question around multi-tenant isolation on Dedicated pools — can you pin models per tenant?
08:42 - Dev Patel: Yes, we support model pinning and can route requests by tenant to dedicated model instances; that helps with noisy neighbor problems.
08:54 - Aminah Farouk: Awesome, sounds promising. Thanks everyone.
09:02 - Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed times for the deep dive. Bye.
09:07 - Dev Patel: Thanks all, bye.
09:10 - Samir Kapoor: Bye.

(Transcript ends — auto-generated, some transcription artifacts expected. See attached links: partner-deck.pdf; benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx; kernel-compatibility-notes.md)
